country.evidence_source: DBs among Korean adolescents decreased in mid-adolescence (14- to 16-years-old) and then increased thereafter in this study. This result was not consistent with previous findings that documented Asian adolescents in Western countries (Le and Stockdale, 2011; Vazsonyi and Keiley, 2007). We speculated that this finding might be due to the measures of DBs used in the current study, which included some status offense items. While the examples of DBs in the study by Le and Stockdale (2011) consisted of carrying a hand gun and selling or supplying drugs such as marijuana, examples of DBs in this study included smoking, drinking alcohol, having sex, and running away from home. These behaviors are illegal for adolescents, but not for adults. According to a recent online survey of Korean adolescents' health status, the smoking and drinking rates of middle school students were 3.3% and 7.4%, respectively, whereas those of high school students were 11.4% and 24.7%, respectively, in Korea (Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, 2015).

Outcome_variable.evidence_source: LS: life satisfaction, DB: delinquent behaviors.

sample_type.evidence_source: The findings of this research study showed that adolescents with high levels of LS at their second year of middle school reported less DBs four years later than adolescents with low levels of LS, even when controlling for important covariates such as initial DBs level, type of family, family income, parents' education, type of high school, and gender.
sample_type.warning: The sample is described as 'Korean adolescents' but no specific recruitment method (e.g., nationally-representative, college students, clinical) is provided, so 'community/convenience' is the best fit.

lag.evidence_source: The aim of the current study was to extend the positive psychology literature by investing the long-term effects of LS on DBs by comparing the bidirectional model between LS and DBs over four years. [...] the findings of this study had higher methodological strength due to the more highly validated analysis design in terms of using four-year longitudinal data and a latent growth model, controlling for various covariates, and comparing the unidirectional and bidirectional models of LS and DBs.
